internal/account-and-email-changes.title: Changing an account email, duplicate accounts, moving submissions between accounts
internal/account-and-email-changes.body:
Email failed to save, cannot change email address, duplicate account, merge two
accounts, two accounts same person, lost access to old institutional email, wrong
email on a submission, submitted under the wrong account.

Distilled from 19 support replies. The public half — why the change is refused, and
what the reader can do — is on **Updating your profile**. This note is the part that
only support can act on, so answers should point people at raising a ticket rather
than describe the mechanics.

**There is no account merge feature.** What actually happens is that submissions are
moved from one account to the other and the spare account is deleted. Answer in terms
of "your submissions can be moved to the account you want to keep", never "we will
merge your accounts", which promises a button that does not exist.

**The cause of "email failed to save" is almost always that the target address already
has an account.** Worth stating plainly, because readers reasonably assume it is a
browser or blocker problem and waste time on that.

**Reviews are not straightforward to move between accounts.** Submissions are. If a
reviewer has completed reviews under the wrong address, the practical fix is usually
to move the submissions rather than the reviews, and to accept some rework.

**An event administrator can change the email address held against a submission
themselves**, from the submissions table. For anyone tied to a single conference this
is faster than coming to us, so route them to their organiser first.

**Where the person has lost access to the old mailbox**, they cannot prove the change
by email, so this always needs support. Expect to confirm both the old and new address
before anything moves.

Do not describe temporary passwords, admin URLs or the internal steps for deleting an
account in an answer. The right answer is always: contact support, say which account
to keep, and it will be sorted.

internal/accounts-emails-and-who-can-cha.title: Accounts and email addresses — who can change what, and why a link shows nothing
internal/accounts-emails-and-who-can-cha.body:
Wrong name showing, change my email address, no role in this event, not registered,
no Oxford Abstracts account, email already exists, merge two accounts, delete my
account, signed in with the wrong address, Google sign-in, single sign-on, blank
dashboard.

Distilled from around 30 support tickets in the year to July 2026. Almost every
"the link doesn't work" ticket is one of these.

**An account must exist, under exactly the right address, before any link works.**
Reviewers, submitters and authors all need to have registered themselves. Assigning
someone submissions does not create an account for them. Until they register, the
reviewer list shows **Not registered**, the submissions table can show **No Oxford
Abstracts account**, and their name is blank — all of which look like faults and are
not. The name fills in the first time they log in.

**"You have no role in this event"** almost always means they are signed in with a
different address from the one on the submission or registration. People who use
Oxford Abstracts for several conferences routinely have two.

**Who can change what:**

- **Names and account email addresses** — only the account holder, from their own
  profile. An admin cannot do it, and neither can support. Name questions you add to
  the submission form are separate fields that an admin *can* edit, but changing them
  does not change the account name.
- **The owner of a submission** — an admin can move a submission to a different
  account from the submissions table. Leave the "send email" box ticked so the new
  owner gets their access link. This is the answer whenever the wrong person needs to
  edit something.
- **A reviewer's email address** — cannot be changed at all. Add the new address as a
  new reviewer and reassign their submissions.
- **Invoices and receipts** — only Oxford Abstracts can amend the name on those.

**Accounts created with Google or another single sign-on** cannot use the ordinary
password reset, and cannot change their email until SSO is removed or a password is
set from the profile page. Google users reset with Google.

**Merging two accounts is not possible** once both exist. The workaround is to move
the submissions to the preferred account, and for reviewing, to add the second address
as a reviewer and reassign.

**An account cannot be deleted while it still holds event content** — the organiser
removes the submission first. Users delete their own account from the profile menu;
support cannot do it for them.

**"Email is invalid" at sign-up** is usually a leading or trailing space in the
address.

internal/api-integrations-and-what-they-.title: The API and the built-in integrations — read-only, and it needs two switches
internal/api-integrations-and-what-they-.body:
API access, GraphQL, connect to another system, EventsAir, Cvent, idloom, push data
into Oxford Abstracts, create submissions through the API, API key, API user, API
costs extra, submission ID in the API.

Distilled from around 15 support tickets in the year to July 2026, on top of the
public API article.

**The API is read-only.** It answers queries; it cannot create submissions, insert
submitters or write data back. Anyone wanting to bring data *into* Oxford Abstracts
has to use the admin interface — an organiser can create a submission on someone's
behalf there. There is **no extra charge** for API access.

**Two switches, not one.** Turning API access on for the event is not enough: the
third party's email address must also be added as an **API user** on the event's API
users page before any request returns data. This is the commonest reason a correctly
built integration sees nothing.

**Field names differ from the screen.** The submission number shown in the admin
interface is `serial_number` in GraphQL, not `id`. Matching on `id` produces numbers
that look wrong.

**There are limits on what is exposed** — email content, for example, is not
available. More complex pulls go through the GraphQL endpoint and its documentation.

**Built-in integrations** exist for **EventsAir**, **Cvent** and a beta **idloom**
integration, each configured on the event's integrations page with instructions on the
page itself. For anything else, the API is the route.

**Single sign-on** is separate from all of this: Google and LinkedIn are standard;
organisation-wide SSO is a paid one-off project covering a client's events, and
everyone reaching those events comes through the client's portal.

internal/assigning-reviewers-and-categor.title: Auto-assign, reviewer categories and why assignment produces nothing
internal/assigning-reviewers-and-categor.body:
Auto assign reviewers, reviewers have no submissions, categories not showing on the
reviewer form, reviewer upload template incompatible, assign by topic, bulk assign
reviewers, unassign incomplete reviews, delete a reviewer.

Distilled from around 20 support tickets in the year to July 2026.

**Categories come from the submission form, and only from a dropdown.** The category
question must be a **single-select dropdown** with the category tag ticked. A
multiple-select dropdown or a checkbox question will not produce assignable
categories — which is why the category field can be missing from the reviewer form
entirely. Only one category question is supported.

**The reviewer form has to carry that category question** before categories will
import against reviewers or appear in the download template.

**Auto-assign matches on category and nothing else.** You set a minimum number of
reviewers per submission, and categories must already be assigned to each reviewer in
the reviewers list. Assignment by any other question, or pairing particular reviewers,
has to be done by hand using the column filters in Reviews by submission. There is no
bulk upload of reviewer-to-submission assignments, and **no undo for a batch**.

**"Re-assign all incomplete reviews"** only touches submissions whose reviews were
never completed. Finished reviews are left alone.

**Things that quietly produce an empty reviewer dashboard:**

- Submissions have not actually been assigned yet — the review count stays at zero.
- The reviewer is listed under an address they have not registered.
- The reviewer was deleted from the list while still holding assignments. Removing a
  reviewer no longer unassigns their submissions, so unassign first, then delete.

**The reviewer upload spreadsheet must match the downloaded template exactly**,
including the parent category column. Extra columns or a stray comma give an
"incompatible" error — open the file in a plain text editor to find it.

**A multi-stage event with a category question in more than one stage** shows every
stage's options on the reviewer sign-up form. Keep the values identical across stages,
or hide the question in the stages you are not using.

**Bulk emails to reviewers fail** unless the reviewer's address is also on the event
users page.

internal/attendees-cannot-edit-their-own.title: Attendees cannot change their own registration answers — the organiser has to amend them
internal/attendees-cannot-edit-their-own.body:
Attendee wants to change their registration, edit my registration answers, change my
dietary requirements, wrong ticket type selected, amend a delegate's details, can
delegates update their own booking, registrant needs to correct their form.

**No.** Once someone has registered, they cannot go back and change the answers they
gave on the registration form. The organiser has to amend the registration on their
behalf, from the registrations table on the event dashboard.

This is a known pain point rather than a setting that is switched off somewhere — it
was raised with the product team in 2026 and is not on the roadmap as of mid-2026,
though the registration module is being looked at. Organisers who ask are usually
spending real time on it, so it is worth saying that the amendment is quick to do
from the table rather than only saying no.

**Two things that are different and do work:**

- **Their own name and email address** — attendees change those themselves from their
  profile page, and admins cannot do it for them.
- **Adding a question after people have registered** — allowed, but the new question
  is not asked of anyone who registered before it existed.

internal/authorize-net-pending-payments.title: Authorize.net payments that are pending or held do not appear in the registrations table
internal/authorize-net-pending-payments.body:
Authorize.net transaction not showing, payment pending in Authorize, charge held for
review, registration missing after payment, transaction in Authorize but not in Oxford
Abstracts, cannot find the registration to apply a payment to.

**Why it happens.** Authorize.net payments are handled differently from invoices and
payment links. Until Authorize confirms the payment, the registration is in the
database but does not appear in the registrations table, so there is nothing on screen
to match the transaction against. A charge held for review by Authorize does the same
thing.

**The workaround support uses:**

1. Create the registration for the person using the **offline invoice** option.
2. Once the money clears in your Authorize account, mark that registration as **Paid**.
3. The registrant gets an email and completes the form as normal.

If the transaction stays stuck rather than merely pending, that is one for support to
pass to the development team — it has happened, and it is not something the organiser
can resolve from the dashboard.

internal/certificates-notes.title: Certificates — quick answers
internal/certificates-notes.body:
Send certificates to presenters only, certificate to some people not all, custom list
of recipients, certificate for presenters in the programme, who gets a certificate.

- **Sending to a chosen group rather than everyone:** the recipient options offer
  broad groups such as accepted presenters, which is not the same as "presenters who
  are actually in the programme". Use the **custom list** option instead, and build
  the address list by exporting from the submissions table with child rows included.
  This is the answer to almost every "I only want certificates to go to X" question.
- **Creating one:** from your Event Dashboard, scroll to the Certificate section in the
  left-hand column and click **Design**.
- **Adding certificates to your plan:** in the admin event portal, use the left-side
  navigation to find Certificates. Click into it and you'll see the option to upgrade
  your plan to include them.
- **Cost:** direct people to oxfordabstracts.com/pricing rather than quoting a figure.

internal/contacting-the-organiser-not-ox.title: You have reached Oxford Abstracts, the software provider — your event organiser handles this
internal/contacting-the-organiser-not-ox.body:
Certificate of participation, attendance certificate, my abstract was rejected, when
will I hear the decision, change my presentation date, refund my registration fee,
programme timetable, accommodation, visa letter, I want to submit my abstract, my
paper, acceptance letter, conference dates — asked of Oxford Abstracts directly by an
attendee, presenter or submitter.

Distilled from 377 support tickets in the year to July 2026 — a quarter of everything
support answers, and by far the largest single pattern in the mailbox.

**What is happening.** Oxford Abstracts makes the software a conference runs on. It
does not run the conference. People who find "Oxford Abstracts" on a confirmation
email often assume it is the organising body, and write asking for things only the
organiser can decide or supply: certificates, decisions, refunds, deadlines,
schedules, or the acceptance of an abstract sent as an email attachment.

**The answer.** Say plainly, and early, that Oxford Abstracts provides the software
and is not involved in running the event, so the question needs the event organiser.
Then help them find the organiser rather than leaving them at a dead end:

- The confirmation or notification email they received carries the organiser's own
  reply-to address — that is the right place to write.
- The conference website or programme page usually lists a contact for the committee
  or secretariat.
- If they are logged in, the event's own pages carry the organiser's contact details.

**Do not** promise to forward the message, confirm a decision, issue a certificate,
change a registration or accept an abstract by email. None of that is Oxford
Abstracts' to give, and a hedged answer produces a second ticket.

**Where it is genuinely ours:** signing in, password resets, verification emails not
arriving, and errors in the software itself. Those are worth separating out — someone
who cannot log in to submit is our problem, while what they submit and whether it is
accepted is not.

**Note for the answer layer.** Around one in twelve of these arrive in Spanish,
French or Portuguese. Answer in the language the question was asked in — the
substance is the same.

internal/coupons-and-group-registration.title: Coupon codes apply to the whole purchase, not to one person in a group booking
internal/coupons-and-group-registration.body:
Coupon code, discount code, promo code, group registration with a coupon, discount
applied to everyone, coupon used by the wrong person, adding a coupon after
registering, coupon not working.

**The behaviour that catches people out.** A coupon discounts the **whole purchase**,
not a named person within it. So when somebody registers a group and enters a code
meant for one of them, everyone on that booking gets the discount.

There is no per-person coupon. If it has already happened, the practical fix is to ask
the person who made the booking who the code was intended for, cancel the other
registrations on it, and have those people register separately.

**Adding a coupon to a registration that already exists** does not need support: open
the registrations table on the event dashboard, find the order, and apply the coupon
there.

**When a code "isn't working"** and it is not the group case above, it is worth asking
for the specific code, the registrant's email address, and a screenshot of the error
before escalating — support cannot diagnose it from the description alone, and that
round trip is most of the delay on these tickets.

internal/dkim-and-sender-verification.title: DKIM added but the sender still shows unverified — domain and address are two steps
internal/dkim-and-sender-verification.body:
DKIM not verifying, added the DKIM record but still unverified, return path not
verified, sender address unverified, verify sender, sending from our own domain,
CNAME and TXT added, DNS records added but nothing changed.

Distilled from support replies in the year to July 2026. The pattern is always the
same: the records are correct and the screen still says unverified.

**Two things verify separately, and both must pass.**

- **The domain** — the DKIM record, and the **return path**, which is a separate
  record people routinely miss. A domain can show DKIM verified and return path not.
- **Each individual sending address** on that domain. Verifying the domain does not
  verify the addresses. Each one gets an email with a link that has to be clicked.

**When an address stays stubbornly unverified**, removing it and adding it again
triggers a fresh confirmation email — that clears most of these.

**DNS propagation is not instant.** Records added within the last day may simply not
have propagated yet, so a re-check tomorrow is a legitimate answer rather than a
brush-off.

**Support can verify manually from their end** once the records are genuinely in
place, and frequently does. If the organiser is confident the DNS is right and the
screen disagrees, that is the escalation — not more DNS edits.

internal/downloading-uploaded-files-and-.title: Bulk downloading uploaded posters, presentations and files, and accepting PowerPoint
internal/downloading-uploaded-files-and-.body:
Download all the posters, bulk download uploaded files, get every presentation,
question response folders, accept PowerPoint uploads, PPT not allowed, collect
slides, download submitted files in one go.

- **Bulk downloading everything people uploaded**: **Abstract management → Reports and
  downloads**, under **Question response folders**. Organisers routinely think they
  have to open submissions one at a time; they do not.
- **Accepting PowerPoint as well as PDF**: use a **file upload** question type on the
  submission form rather than a poster upload question. The poster gallery itself
  takes single-page PDFs, but a file upload question will take slide decks.
- **File type and size limits** are per question type and are listed on the submission
  question types guide, under the multimedia questions section — worth quoting the
  actual limits rather than guessing, because they differ by question type.

internal/emails-templates-and-merge-fiel.title: Which emails send automatically, and what merge fields can and cannot do
internal/emails-templates-and-merge-fiel.body:
Automatic emails, chase incomplete submissions, email selected submitters, merge field
not working, submission edit link, test email shows empty links, email authors and
submitters together, notify admins of new submissions, attach a file to an email,
resend the confirmation email.

Distilled from around 20 support tickets in the year to July 2026.

**Only the templates at the top of the emails page send automatically**, they fire on
submission, and they always go to **submitters only**. Everything else — chasing
incomplete submissions, telling people about decisions, reminding presenters — is a
manual send, either from the emails page or by selecting rows in a table.

**Tables are how you reach anyone who is not a submitter:** the decisions table for
authors and presenters, the envelope icon on the registrations table for delegates.
Filter the decisions table on decision and registration status to email, say, accepted
presenters who have not yet registered. You cannot email submitters and authors in one
send; do the two groups separately.

**Merge fields:**

- **A test email does not populate merge fields**, so links look empty. Send to a real
  or test submission to check one properly.
- There are **two link fields**: the submission link, and the **submission edit link**
  which drops the person straight into their own submission to amend it.
- **Form responses cannot be merged** into automatic templates — this is by design.
  Point people to their dashboard, or email manually from the submission table.
- **A question hidden in a stage will not merge** into that stage's emails. Set it to
  **read only** instead of hidden and the value still appears.
- There is **no merge field for the stage name** — make a template per stage and type
  it.
- **Reviewer comments cannot be merged** into notification emails; submitters read
  them on their dashboard.

**Notifying admins of each new submission:** add the notification addresses on Event
setup → Event details, then open the relevant template and tick the CC or BCC option
for conference notification emails at the bottom.

**Things that cannot be changed:**

- The **"submission created"** email fires at the moment of submission and cannot be
  re-sent. A manual email is the alternative, without the personalised detail.
- The **reviewer recruitment** confirmation and the **certificate** email have fixed
  wording shared across all events. Follow up with an "email selected" message from
  the reviewers list instead.
- A **deleted email template cannot be restored.**

**Attachments** on a template reach the recipient as a link to the file in Oxford
Abstracts, not as an attached file.

**Emails send from the event name with the notification address as reply-to** unless
you verify your own sender address — see the DKIM note.

internal/event-setup-notes.title: Event setup — quick answers
internal/event-setup-notes.body:
Book a support session, speak to someone, demo, phone number, set up a new event for
me, image dimensions, picture sizes, upgrade my plan.

- **Booking time with the team** is the answer to a surprising share of tickets — over
  40 in the year to July 2026 ended with it. Organisers can book a free one-to-one
  support session or a product demonstration through the online booking calendar at
  any time. There is **no telephone support line**; email or a booked session are the
  two routes.
- **Having Oxford Abstracts set up a new event** needs four things in the email: the
  organisation name, the event name, the event abbreviation (for example ABC2026), and
  the event notification email address, which must be one of the organiser's own.
- **Recommended image dimensions** for banners, logos and backgrounds are published in
  the help centre; using them avoids pixelated or cropped uploads.
- **Background image dimensions** for the event theme: 1920 x 600px.
- **Upgrading a plan:** direct people to the support/sales team rather than describing
  the steps.
- **Pricing questions:** see the dedicated pricing note — always oxfordabstracts.com/pricing,
  never a quoted figure.
- **Speaking to a human:** the contact form is the route; support replies as soon as they can.

internal/events-clients-admins-and-copyi.title: Creating next year's event, copying one, and who can see which events
internal/events-clients-admins-and-copyi.body:
Create a new event, next year's conference, copy a previous event, clone an event,
cannot see the new event option, client admin, event admin, super admin, past events
missing, reuse last year's event, organisation name on invoices.

Distilled from around 20 support tickets in the year to July 2026.

**Creating events needs client admin rights.** If a dashboard only offers submitting
or reviewing, the account does not have them. Client admins create events themselves
from the client's new-event page — they do not need to ask support.

**Copying is the normal way to start a new year.** Creating a new event offers a copy
of a previous one, bringing across submission and review forms, email templates and
reviewers. Points that catch people out:

- **Free events cannot be copied** and have to be built from the default questions.
- **Check you are under the right client.** A duplicate client account leaves you
  copying an unused event with only the default form.
- **Copying brings no data** — submissions cannot be moved between events.
- Old sessions, dates, tracks and column names come across too, and are cleared from
  the programme builder Settings menus, sessions individually via the trash icon.

**A past event cannot be reopened and reused for a new year.** Pricing is per
conference, so a new setup is needed. The new event carries a "pay for event" link
which generates the invoice and grants access straight away so work can begin.

**Who sees what:**

- **Client (master) admins** see every event under the organisation.
- **Event admins** see only their own event, not others on the same client account.
- **Super admins** do not appear in an event's admin list because they have access to
  everything; they are managed from the client dashboard.
- Your events may sit under **more than one client account** — if past events seem
  missing, switch client accounts.

Client admins are added and removed on the client admins page, event admins on the
event's admin users page. Support cannot add an admin without approval from an
existing admin.

**Running admin and submitter roles on one account does not work** — you cannot switch
an admin account into the submitter view. Use a second address, or edit the submission
as an admin in the table.

**The organisation name on the account and invoices** is edited on the client edit
page.

**The event abbreviation cannot contain special characters** — they break merge
fields.

internal/example-autosave.title: Does the submission form save automatically?
internal/example-autosave.body:
Yes — responses to each question save when you move to the next field, and the
submission stays available as incomplete if you close the tab. There is no
Save button; that's by design. Submitters can log back in and continue from
their dashboard.

internal/exhibitor-booths.title: Exhibitor booths — changing the linked email address and the wrong name showing
internal/exhibitor-booths.body:
Exhibitor booth wrong email, change the exhibitor contact, wrong name showing on a
booth, exhibitor cannot access their booth, exhibitor representative name incorrect,
sponsor booth setup.

Exhibitor space is a Professional Conference feature. Distilled from support replies
in the year to July 2026.

- **Changing the email address linked to a booth:** on the event dashboard's
  **Exhibitors** page, click into the row and change the email. The new address then
  has access to set the booth up, and the old one loses it. Organisers assume this
  needs support; it does not.
- **A wrong name appearing against a booth** is usually the display name on the
  account behind that email address, not a booth setting — the exhibitor set it when
  they registered, and it follows them. The person changes it from their own profile.
  Where the account itself is wrong, support can delete it so they can register again,
  but check with the exhibitor first: anything else attached to that account goes too.
- **Booth images:** there are recommended dimensions for picture uploads; point people
  at the guide rather than letting them guess, because a badly sized image is the
  commonest complaint after access.

internal/exports-reports-and-abstract-bo.title: Exports, custom reports and abstract books — child rows, columns and empty books
internal/exports-reports-and-abstract-bo.body:
Export author details, download the submission table, child rows, spreadsheet builder,
custom report, abstract book empty, book contains only titles, presenter email list,
export missing columns, registration export.

Distilled from around 25 support tickets in the year to July 2026.

**Child rows are the answer to most export questions.** Author names, affiliations,
emails, presenting status and registration status all live on the *child rows* of a
submission. Export the submissions table **with child rows** and each author appears
as their own row. A presenter list is that export filtered on the presenting column.
Without child rows you get the submitter only.

**Exports contain the columns you can see.** On the submissions and decisions tables,
use the **Columns** button to switch fields on before downloading, because the export
mirrors the current view. The **registration table behaves the opposite way** — the
column filter changes only the screen, and the download always contains every column,
so unwanted ones have to be deleted afterwards.

**The spreadsheet builder** lets you pick exactly which fields appear in a custom
Excel report, and is the right route when no standard report has the combination you
need. It cannot reach the registration table, and registration status is not among its
fields.

**An accepted-abstracts book downloads empty until decisions have actually been made.**
The "all abstracts" reports still contain data, so an empty accepted book is usually
a decisions problem rather than a book problem. If submissions are missing from a book
or custom report, look for an unanswered dependency question.

**A book containing nothing but titles** is the per-question **In abstract book**
checkbox, unticked. See the note on question checkboxes.

**Two book tools exist:** the custom book builder, which offers grouping and sorting
(by acceptance type, first author surname and so on), and the more advanced book
builder where you edit the template and use *Save as* to keep a named version. Oxford
Abstracts can also build bespoke books and reports on request — these then appear as
extra headings on the event's Reports and downloads page. Complex ones may carry a
development cost.

**Two export oddities worth knowing:** the registered-date column comes out as text
because it carries date, time and timezone together, so strip the time to sort
chronologically; and TRUE/FALSE in an export is simply the system's yes/no.

internal/finding-your-oxford-abstracts-i.title: Where do I pay Oxford Abstracts, or find my own invoice?
internal/finding-your-oxford-abstracts-i.body:
Your own Oxford Abstracts bill — not your attendees' — is on the **Event payments**
page. Reach it from the **credit card icon in the top bar**, to the left of your
account initial, on any page inside the event. It lists each payment with its type,
the date created, the date paid, and a reference number, and carries a **Make
payment** link.

This is a different thing from the invoices your attendees receive for their
registration tickets, which live under **Registration**. Both are called "invoices",
which is why the question arrives ambiguously: someone asking where their invoice is
may mean either. If they mention paying Oxford Abstracts, a package, credit or an
overdue account, they mean this page.

The icon is easy to miss — it is unlabelled — so saying where it is, rather than
just naming the page, is usually the difference between an answered question and a
second ticket.

internal/invoice-due-dates-and-losing-ac.title: Payment overdue on screen while the invoice says otherwise — two different dates
internal/invoice-due-dates-and-losing-ac.body:
Payment overdue message, invoice due date does not match, locked out after upgrading,
features unavailable while waiting for payment, extend the payment deadline, paying by
invoice removed my access, event says payment overdue.

**They are two separate dates and they are not linked.** The event has a payment due
date that controls access to paid features; the invoice has its own due date, and an
invoice can be regenerated at any time. So a screen can say payment is overdue while
the invoice in the organiser's hand says it is not due until next week. This is not a
billing error and not a fault.

**What to do:** support extends the event's payment due date to match the invoice.
That restores access immediately. Organisations waiting on a finance department or a
purchase order should ask for the extension rather than hurrying the payment — this is
routine and support does it readily.

**Nothing is lost while access is restricted.** Website-builder work, event setup and
submissions are all still there and reappear the moment payment or an extension goes
through. Say this early: the fear of losing work is what turns a billing question into
an urgent ticket.

**Related but different:** an expired *trial* cannot be reactivated without payment,
though the work on it is likewise still there afterwards.

internal/multi-stage-events.title: Multi-stage events — renaming stages, moving submissions, and what the add-on covers
internal/multi-stage-events.body:
Multi stage, second stage, rename a stage, change the stage title, move submissions
between stages, multi-stage add-on cost, is multi stage switched on, full paper stage
after abstracts, two-stage review.

Distilled from support replies in the year to July 2026.

- **Renaming a stage** is done on the **Event details** page of the event dashboard,
  at any time. Organisers hunt for it inside the stage itself and do not find it.
- **Moving submissions between stages** is done from the **Decisions** screen, not the
  submissions table.
- **Multi-stage is a separately purchased add-on.** It can be switched off, and an
  event that had it last year may not have it now — worth checking before treating
  "the stages have disappeared" as a fault. Support enables it once purchased.
- **Reviewer data does not travel between stages.** A second-stage reviewer cannot see
  what the first-stage reviewers wrote; only event admins can. If the committee needs
  that continuity, an admin has to carry it across by hand.
- **A second round of reviews on moved submissions** works normally once the
  submissions are in the new stage.

internal/network-blocks-and-login-troubl.title: Network failure, page will not load, failed to fetch — usually the network, not us
internal/network-blocks-and-login-troubl.body:
Network failure, failed to fetch, page cannot be displayed, dashboard will not load,
checkbox will not tick, error parsing response, cannot open the review link, spinner
never stops, works on my phone but not the office computer.

Distilled from around 30 support tickets in the year to July 2026 — the most common
"it is broken" report, and usually not a fault in the software.

**Work down this list before escalating. It resolves most of them:**

1. **An incognito or private window.** A cached session or a second signed-in account
   is the commonest single cause, and this rules it out in seconds.
2. **A different network — mobile data is the quickest test.** University and hospital
   firewalls block Oxford Abstracts often enough that "Network Failure" on the
   submission or sign-up page should be read as a network block until proved
   otherwise. The fix on their side is asking IT to allow the domain.
3. **Chrome on a desktop**, rather than an unusual or very old browser.
4. **Clear the cache**, or try another device.

**Go direct rather than through the dashboard.** A reviewer who cannot get past the
dashboard can often open their review form straight from the stage review URL, and a
submitter can reach a form from its stage submitter URL. If a link in a notification
email will not open, the dashboard always holds their submissions and feedback.

**What to gather if none of that works:** the exact error text, the URL they were on,
the email address they signed in with, and whether it happens on another network. An
error quoting an internal `/purs-api/...` path is a genuine application error worth
passing on — the rest of the list above is not.

internal/not-currently-possible.title: Things Oxford Abstracts does not currently support
internal/not-currently-possible.body:
Not possible, not supported, cannot be done, is there a way to, does the system allow,
QR code per delegate, reset submission numbering, edit an invoice, attendees editing
their own registration, redirect the homepage, host a template file.

Confirmed limitations. Answer these plainly — a clear "no" is more useful than a
workaround that doesn't exist.

- **Changing fonts** — you cannot change fonts on Oxford Abstracts software.
- **Visa / invitation letters** — there is no feature to generate visa support letters.
  Submitters asking about this should contact their event administrator.
- **DOIs** — Digital Object Identifiers are not supported.
- **Duplicating or cloning a question** — not possible.
- **Importing sessions in bulk / via CSV** — not possible at this time.
- **Italics on the review form** — not available.
- **Changing the "Get tickets" button wording** — the button text cannot be changed.
- **Hyperlinks in a ticket description** — not currently possible, but planned.
- **Checking for duplicate IDs in the programme** — not supported. Workaround:
  Conference > Program > Sessions > Submission IDs.
- **Group tickets** — you cannot buy a "group" ticket, but an attendee can buy multiple
  tickets and name the other ticket holders on the registration form.
- **A mobile app** — there is no Oxford Abstracts app.
- **Re-running auto-assign for some submissions only** — re-running auto-assign
  re-assigns all submissions.
- **Committee members building the programme** — only admin users can create sessions
  and allocate presentations to them.
- **Multiple users editing the same abstract** — only the person who submitted it can edit it.
- **Admins changing a reviewer's email** — reviewers must change it themselves from their
  own account.
- **Admins changing an attendee's name** — attendees do this from their profile page.
- **Admins changing a submitter's email address** — only the submitter can, from
  My Profile.
- **Authors and affiliations on the decisions table** — that data appears only on the
  Submissions table accordion rows, not the Decisions page.

Added from a year of support replies, July 2026:

- **A QR code or barcode per registrant** — not possible. The system produces one
  common code for the whole programme, not an individual code on each delegate's name
  badge. This is the single most-asked limitation, and there is no workaround inside
  Oxford Abstracts.
- **Resetting submission numbering** — not possible. Deleting a submission does not
  truly delete it, so its number is never released and the sequence keeps counting.
- **Attendees editing their own registration answers** — attendees cannot go back and
  change what they entered; the organiser has to amend it for them. Not on the roadmap
  as of mid-2026, though it has been raised with the product team. (They *can* change
  their own name and email from their profile page — that is different.)
- **Editing an invoice or receipt yourself** — organisers cannot change the name,
  organisation or line items on an issued invoice or receipt. Oxford Abstracts support
  has to make the edit; ask them, then download the corrected file from the
  registrations table.
- **Redirecting the conference homepage to a website-builder site** — not possible.
  Hide the conference homepage instead; see the website builder note.
- **Hosting a downloadable file, such as a Word template, on the submission form** —
  the form can only link out to an external URL, so the file has to live somewhere
  else (your own site, a shared drive) and be linked from there.

From a further pass over the same year's replies, July 2026:

- **A full audit log or change history** — the submissions table has a **last updated
  by** column naming the most recent editor, but there is no history of earlier edits
  and no record of which admin changed event details.
- **Renaming or reordering stages once created** — the only route is new stages, move
  the submissions, delete the old ones, which is unwise once submissions exist.
- **Hiding an individual session** from the public programme — publish or unpublish
  the whole programme only.
- **Duplicating a question** on the submission form, and only one authors question and
  one category question per form.
- **A second review form** — one per stage. Different criteria per category need
  separate stages.
- **Rejection sub-types** — only acceptance supports types. The decision list itself
  (Pending, Accepted, Rejected, Withdrawn) is fixed and cannot be switched off.
- **Sponsor levels beyond Gold, Silver and Bronze** — hard coded and shared by every
  event, so they cannot be renamed or added to. Only one sponsor shows in the
  programme side menu.
- **Bulk importing registrations**, and **no check-in function** at the event.
- **Guest ticket checkout** — anyone buying a ticket must register or log in.
- **Embedding the submission form** in an iframe; only the programme can be embedded.
- **URL redirects** for programme pages.
- **Bulk changing abstract titles** between sentence and title case — one at a time in
  the submissions table.
- **Capping submissions per submission type** — monitor and hide the option when full.
- **Telephone support** — email, or book a support session.

internal/only-the-submitter-can-see-or-e.title: Co-authors, presenters and panellists cannot see or edit the submission
internal/only-the-submitter-can-see-or-e.body:
Co-author cannot see the abstract, presenter cannot upload their slides, my colleague
cannot find the submission, supervisor needs to edit, panellist wants to add a file,
nothing on my dashboard, transfer a submission to someone else.

Distilled from around 15 support tickets in the year to July 2026 — a rule that
surprises people every time.

**Only the submitter has the submission.** It appears on their dashboard and nobody
else's. Co-authors, presenters, panellists and supervisors named on an abstract cannot
see it, cannot edit it, and cannot upload files to it, even when they have their own
Oxford Abstracts account. A direct link to a submission only works for the person who
created it.

**When somebody else needs control**, an admin changes the owner of the submission
from the submissions table. That moves all correspondence to the new person too.

**Practical consequences worth saying out loud:**

- A panellist who wants to add their own slides must either send the file to the
  submitter, or make their own separate submission — which gives them their own
  submission ID.
- Co-authors only ever reach the system through the automatic email sent by **part 3**
  of the authors and affiliations question, which asks them their own extra questions.
  That link is the only thing they can open.
- Whether a co-author or presenter has registered for the event is visible to the
  organiser: open the submissions table, click **Show authors**, and read the paid
  status on the accordion rows.
- There is no automatic email asking co-authors to supply their details beyond that
  part 3 link; anything else has to be a manual email.

internal/password-reset-and-sign-in-prob.title: Password reset not arriving, or resetting on the wrong site — sign-in problems
internal/password-reset-and-sign-in-prob.body:
Password reset email not arriving, reset link not working, cannot log in, forgot my
password, reviewer cannot sign in, reset link expired, no reset email received,
unable to access my account, submission portal login.

Distilled from 22 support tickets in the year to July 2026 — the largest access
problem after reviewers not seeing their assignments.

**Check the site first — this is the commonest cause and nobody spots it.** There are
two Oxford Abstracts sites with logins, and people reset the wrong one:

- **app.oxfordabstracts.com** — the actual software: submitting, reviewing,
  registering, running an event. Reset here:
  **https://app.oxfordabstracts.com/auth/forgot-password**
- **help.oxfordabstracts.com** — this help centre. Its own reset page does nothing for
  the app, and someone who lands there will keep resetting a password that was never
  the problem.

If the reset link in an email came from the help centre, that is the fault.

**Then work down these:**

1. **The email is slow or filtered.** Ask them to check spam and wait a few minutes,
   then request it again from the app address above.
2. **They are trying a different address from the one on the account.** Someone using
   Oxford Abstracts for more than one conference often has two. Reviewers especially —
   the organiser assigns one address and the reviewer signs in with another.
3. **A stale session.** An incognito or private window rules this out in seconds and
   fixes a surprising number of cases.

**Support can reset a password manually** if none of that works. The person then
changes it themselves after signing in, from their profile page.

**One thing that is not the cause:** an organiser cannot reset a submitter's or
reviewer's password, and cannot change their email address. That has to come from the
account holder or from support.

internal/pricing-and-plans.title: How much does Oxford Abstracts cost? Pricing, plans and packages
internal/pricing-and-plans.body:
Cost, price, pricing, plans, packages, Basic, Abstract Management, Standard or
Professional Conference Package, Symposia, Certificates, add-ons, upgrading, free
version: always point at https://oxfordabstracts.com/pricing

Those first lines are what the router sees — `api/search.js` sends a note's title
plus only the opening 160 characters of its body — so the plan names have to sit at
the very top or a question naming one routes to that plan's feature articles
instead, and comes back with no answer at all.

**The answer to any pricing question is the pricing page: https://oxfordabstracts.com/pricing**

It lists the current price of every plan and add-on. Give the reader that link and
tell them what they will find there. **Never quote a figure, a price band, or a
per-abstract cost** — those go stale, and a wrong number in a help answer is worse
than no number.

Do not send pricing questions to accounts@oxfordabstracts.com. That address is for
paying in an alternative currency, not for finding out what something costs.

The plans, cheapest first, are: **Basic** (free), **Abstract Management**,
**Standard Conference Package** and **Professional Conference Package**.
**Certificates**, **Symposia** and **Multi-stage** are bought separately, and
Certificates is included with Professional.

You also see the price for your own event when you create it, before you pay.

internal/programme-and-homepage-notes.title: Programme and conference homepage — quick answers
internal/programme-and-homepage-notes.body:
- **Attendees reach the conference homepage** by logging into your event portal — it's the
  first page they land on.
- **Adding a link inside a programme session:** Program builder → open the session →
  Add a description → Insert link icon → paste your link.
- **Committee members cannot build the programme** — admin users only.

internal/programme-builder-sessions-and-.title: Programme builder — sessions, publishing, access and what cannot be customised
internal/programme-builder-sessions-and-.body:
Publish the programme, programme not visible, hide a session, parallel sessions,
tracks, session chairs, move a presentation to another session, embed the programme,
programme filters, no PDF of the programme, programme codes.

Distilled from around 30 support tickets in the year to July 2026.

**Publishing controls everything.** An unpublished programme is visible only to
admins, and an embedded programme will keep asking viewers to log in until it is
published — setting open access is not enough on its own. You can publish and
unpublish as often as you like. Access type (open, login required, invited only) is
set under Programme builder → Settings.

**Sessions:**

- Every session needs a date and time before it can be created; both can change later.
  Old dates left over from a copied event are cleared in Settings → Dates.
- To move a presentation, **unassign** it from its current session first, then assign
  it to the new one.
- To place many abstracts at once, copy the submission IDs from the submissions table
  and bulk assign them.
- Parallel sessions are built with **columns**, limiting each session to a column.
  There is no limit on how many run concurrently.
- A session takes only **one track**, though it can hold many submissions.
- **Chairs are entirely separate from authors and presenters.** They are entered
  manually in the programme builder and are never matched to a person of the same name.
  There is no chair report — export the sessions table and remove duplicate rows.
- To put a speaker in a session, add them as an ordinary submission and attach it.

**Things that cannot be changed, because the layout is shared by every event:**

- Individual sessions cannot be hidden; only the whole programme can be unpublished.
- The filters across the top of the public programme cannot be switched off. The topic
  and track filters do come from submission questions, so unticking the category label
  on that question removes it as a filter.
- The order and arrangement of items cannot be customised.
- There are no URL redirects for programme pages. Embed the programme URL in an iframe
  on your own site instead; only the whole programme can be embedded, not a section.

**There is no direct PDF of the programme.** Download the docx from the programme
builder and convert it, export the sessions table to Excel, or take the programme from
the public front end. Programme builder downloads are Word only and admin only.

**Programme codes** are assigned with the assign-codes tool or by hand in the
decisions table, and replace the submission ID in the programme. Bulk assignment needs
the Standard or Professional package — it is not on Abstract Management.

internal/qr-codes-and-name-badges.title: QR codes and barcodes on delegate name badges — one per event, not one per person
internal/qr-codes-and-name-badges.body:
QR code for each registrant, barcode per delegate, unique QR code per attendee,
scanning delegates in, name tag with a barcode, badge scanning, check-in by QR,
individual QR codes, can the system generate QR codes.

The most-asked limitation of the year: 17 support tickets in the twelve months to
July 2026, more than any other "can it do this" question.

**No — not per person.** Oxford Abstracts cannot generate an individual QR code or
barcode for each registrant to carry on their badge. What it produces is a single
common code for the whole programme, which anyone can scan to reach the event.

There is no workaround inside Oxford Abstracts, so say so plainly rather than
offering a half-answer. Organisers who need per-delegate scanning — for session
attendance, entry control or lead capture — do it with a separate badge-printing or
check-in service, feeding it an export of the attendee list from the registrations
table.

Do not confuse this with the name badge content itself, which is configurable in the
usual way; the limitation is specifically the per-person code.

internal/question-checkboxes-show-to-rev.title: Reviewers, books or the programme showing only the title — the per-question checkboxes
internal/question-checkboxes-show-to-rev.body:
Reviewers only see the title, abstract book contains just titles, uploaded file not
showing in the programme, question missing from the book, reviewer cannot see the
abstract, content not appearing, show to reviewer, in books, in program.

The single most common configuration problem in the support mailbox, in several
disguises. Distilled from around 15 tickets in the year to July 2026.

**Every question on the submission form has its own checkboxes at the bottom of the
question editor**, and each controls one destination:

- **Show to reviewer** — whether reviewers see that answer. If reviewers report seeing
  only the title and category, this is switched off on the other questions. It is a
  per-question setting, not a limitation of the free package, and not a fault.
- **In abstract book** — whether the answer appears in the downloadable books. A book
  that comes out containing nothing but titles is this, on every other question.
- **Program** — whether the answer, including an uploaded file, appears in the online
  programme.

Open the question in **Submission form editor** and tick the ones you need. They are
independent of one another: a question can be visible to reviewers and absent from the
book, or the reverse.

**Two related traps in the same editor:**

- **Reviewers seeing "untitled submission" or bare ID numbers** means either "Show to
  reviewers" is off on the title question, or the wrong field has been set as the
  title question for that stage.
- **A confirmation email showing the whole abstract instead of the title** means the
  title setting has been applied to the wrong question. Move it to the actual title
  question.

internal/registration-and-fees-notes.title: Registration and fees — quick answers
internal/registration-and-fees-notes.body:
Paying by card, credit card, payment link, offline payment, mark as paid, Authorize.net
pending, registration not showing, invoice wrong name, trial expired, registration
error, special characters in address.

- **Service fee on refunds:** Oxford Abstracts does not reimburse the service fee if an
  order is refunded.
- **Submitting is not registering:** submitting an abstract does not register someone for
  the event. They must buy a ticket separately.
- **Payment links** are sent to the ticket buyer and any other recipients of the invoice,
  by email, and can also be reached from the ticket buyer's dashboard.
- **Printing a delegate list with addresses:** from the Registrations tab, download the
  table data with the download button, then manipulate and print as needed.
- **Editing the registration form after delegates have submitted:** yes, you can — but
  questions added afterwards will not appear for people who already submitted.
- **Authorize.net errors:** direct these to the support team.
- **PCI / attestation of compliance:** support can email this on request.

From a year of support replies, July 2026:

- **Paying by card:** organisers do not need a payment link from support. From the
  event dashboard, click the card icon and choose the card payment method. You have to
  be signed in as the account that owns the event.
- **The "offline payment" option** means the money moves outside Oxford Abstracts
  entirely. Once it lands in your own account, the organiser marks that registration as
  **Paid** by hand. Registrations sitting unpaid are usually this, not a fault.
- **Authorize.net payments held or pending** do not appear in the registrations table
  at all, because Authorize handles payments differently from invoices and payment
  links. Workaround: create the registration using the offline invoice option, then mark
  it paid once the money clears. The registrant gets an email and completes the form.
- **A trial that has expired** cannot be reactivated without payment — but nothing is
  lost. Website-builder work and event setup are all still there and reappear as soon
  as the upgrade goes through. Say this early; the fear of losing work is what drives
  the ticket.
- **Registration failing with an odd error** is often the address field: very long
  addresses, and commas inside them, can break it. Ask them to shorten it and remove
  commas before escalating.
- **Editing an invoice or receipt** (wrong name, wrong organisation) has to be done by
  Oxford Abstracts support — organisers cannot. Once support has amended it, download
  the corrected copy from the registrations table.

internal/reviewer-comments-what-submitte.title: Inline comments versus comments to the author — why submitters see nothing
internal/reviewer-comments-what-submitte.body:
Authors cannot see reviewer comments, inline comments not showing to submitters,
feedback missing, show reviews to submitters turned on but nothing appears, hide
comments from some submitters, inline comments missing from the Excel export.

**There are two separate places a reviewer can leave feedback**, and this is almost
always the answer when submitters say they can see nothing:

1. **"Comments to the author"** — a field on the review form.
2. **Inline comments** — notes attached to specific points in the text.

Turning on "inline comments visible to submitters" reveals only the second kind. If the
reviewers actually typed into "Comments to the author", the submitters will see nothing
even though the setting is on and everything looks correct. Check which one the
reviewers used before treating it as a fault — in every ticket of this shape so far,
the reviewers had used the other field.

**Showing comments is all or nothing.** You cannot reveal feedback to some submitters
and withhold it from others. The setting is on or off for everyone.

**Inline comments do not come out in the Excel export.** Only the general comments do.
Anyone building a spreadsheet of feedback needs to know that before they promise it to
a committee.

internal/reviewers-cannot-see-reviews.title: A reviewer cannot see their assigned reviews or submissions
internal/reviewers-cannot-see-reviews.body:
Reviewer cannot see assigned reviews, no submissions showing, reviewer dashboard
empty, "you have not been assigned to any reviews", reviewer shows as unregistered,
reviewer cannot access abstracts to review, reviewer sees IDs but no titles.

Distilled from 24 support replies to this exact problem. Work down the list — the
first two causes account for most of them.

**1. They are signed in with a different email address.** By far the most common
cause. The reviewer must sign in with the exact address the organiser assigned. A
reviewer who uses Oxford Abstracts for more than one conference often has two
addresses. Check the address shown top-right against the one in the By Reviewer
table.

**2. They have not registered yet.** The By Reviewer table shows **unregistered**
against their name until they do. Assigning submissions does not create an account —
they must register themselves, with that same address, at
app.oxfordabstracts.com. The name auto-fills once the account exists.

**3. Reviewing is not open for that stage.** Reviews only appear while the stage is
open. On a multi-stage event, check the specific stage rather than the event.

**4. The account is linked to Google or LinkedIn.** Unlinking it from the profile
page resolves it; see the profile article.

**5. An email alias.** An alias needs its own Oxford Abstracts account, and the
alias itself has to be on the reviewer list — it does not inherit from the main
address.

**6. The review form has no required question.** Reviews then auto-complete the
moment they are assigned, so there is nothing left to review. Make at least one
question required.

**7. Reviewers see ID numbers instead of titles.** The wrong question is set as the
title question on the submission form.

If none of that applies, support's usual last resort is to remove the reviewer from
the reviewer list, re-add them and reassign the submissions. Unassigning does not
delete review data — a completed review reappears as completed once the submission
is reassigned.

**Reviewers who contact Oxford Abstracts directly should be sent to their event
administrator** — the address is shown under the conference name on their dashboard.
Oxford Abstracts does not run the events and cannot change an event's settings.

internal/reviewing-notes.title: Reviewing — quick answers
internal/reviewing-notes.body:
Adding reviewers in bulk fails, duplicate email addresses, paste a list of reviewers,
second stage reviewers cannot see first stage comments, can co-authors see the reviews,
who sees reviewer feedback, unassign incomplete reviewers.

- **Reviewers are not emailed automatically** when they are added to the system. You have
  to notify them yourself.
- **Preparing decisions during reviewing:** yes, you can start preparing decisions while
  reviewing is still ongoing.
- **Undoing a bulk decision:** reselect the submissions and choose a different decision
  type.
- **Auto-assign is all-or-nothing:** re-running it re-assigns every submission, not just
  some.

From a year of support replies, July 2026:

- **Adding a list of reviewers silently fails if the list contains a duplicate email
  address.** The whole import stops rather than skipping the repeat. Ask them to
  de-duplicate the list and try again — this is the first thing to check when a bulk
  add "just doesn't work", and organisers rarely spot it themselves.
- **Reviewers in a later stage cannot see reviews from an earlier one.** Reviewer data
  from previous stages is visible only to event admins, so a second-stage reviewer
  reading a full paper cannot see what the abstract reviewers said. If the committee
  needs that continuity, an admin has to carry it across.
- **Co-authors never see reviewer feedback**, and cannot see the abstract either. Only
  the submitter can, and only if the organiser has turned on showing reviews to
  submitters.
- **Unassigning everyone who did not complete their review** can be done in one go from
  the reviews table; reassigning to sweep-up reviewers afterwards is manual.

internal/security-compliance-and-data-re.title: Security questionnaires, compliance documents and how long data is kept
internal/security-compliance-and-data-re.body:
ISO 27001, penetration test, security questionnaire, VPAT, HECVAT, PCI compliance,
SAQ AOC, accessibility statement, procurement review, data retention, how long do you
keep our data, audit log, GDPR.

Distilled from support replies in the year to July 2026. These arrive from procurement
and IT teams rather than organisers, and a straight answer saves a long thread.

**Certification.** Oxford Abstracts does **not** hold ISO 27001 certification and does
not have a formal third-party penetration test report. What it does have is a
documented Information Security Policy covering encryption at rest and in transit,
multi-factor authentication on the AWS infrastructure, role-based access control that
isolates each client's data, access and audit logging with regular credential
rotation, and Cloudflare and AWS WAF protection. Say this plainly — the absence of ISO
27001 is not a secret and a vague answer invites more questions.

**Documents available on request:** a VPAT, a HECVAT, a PCI compliance certificate and
an SAQ AOC. Ask support.

**Contract renewals.** Where the Standard Terms and Conditions have not changed since
an agreement was executed, the existing agreement remains valid at renewal — no new
signature or re-execution is needed.

**Retention.** Events stay accessible for at least a year after the event has
finished, and packages cover a single event. **Registration data is not retained for
past events, and deleted data cannot be recovered**, whereas submission data from past
events does remain. Anyone who needs registration records long-term should export them
while the event is live.

**There is no full audit log, but there is one column worth knowing about.** The
submissions table carries **last updated by**, which names the most recent editor of
each submission. That is the whole of it: no history of earlier edits, no record of
what the previous version said, and no log of which admin changed event details such
as dates. So the column answers "who touched this last" but never "what did this
abstract originally say". Organisers who need that should download the submissions
table on a schedule and keep the files.

**ISBNs** for published abstracts are not something Oxford Abstracts can issue; in the
UK those come from Nielsen.

internal/submission-form-open-closed-and.title: \"New submissions are closed\" or a greyed-out Edit button — the form's separate switches
internal/submission-form-open-closed-and.body:
New submissions are currently closed, cannot submit, edit button greyed out, edits
disabled for this submission, submitters cannot amend, reopen the form, let people
edit after the deadline, submission link not working, ineligible to submit.

Distilled from around 12 support tickets in the year to July 2026.

**The form is not one switch, it is several**, all on the event dashboard, and they
are the cause of nearly every "my submitters cannot do X" report:

- **New** — accepts new submissions. If this is off but the editing switches are on,
  submitters see *"Sorry, new submissions are currently closed for this event"*.
- **Edit complete** — lets submitters change a finished submission.
- **Edit incomplete** — lets them go back and finish an unfinished one.

A greyed-out or disabled **Edit** button, or *"Edits disabled for this submission"*,
is the relevant editing switch being off. Opening a form for editing opens it for
**everyone**, so export the submissions table first as a backup; for a single person,
it is usually easier for an admin to make the change in the submissions table instead.

**To let people revise without accepting new work**, turn the editing switches on and
leave **New** off, then send them the same submission link. They must sign in with the
address they originally used.

**"Your email address has not been permitted to submit"** means the stage is set to
*only allow specified email addresses* with none added — which blocks everybody.
Either switch it to allow anyone, or add the permitted addresses.

**The submission link is per stage**, of the form `.../stages/<id>/submitter`, and is
copied from Submissions → Form & setup. An old or mistyped link gives a
form-not-found error.

**A deadline written as "to 1 April" runs until 23:59 on 1 April.** The exact
auto-closure time and its timezone are shown by clicking the time on the dashboard.

**Always test as a non-admin.** Admin accounts see more and behave differently, so a
form that works for you can be shut to everyone else.

internal/submissions-notes.title: Submissions — quick answers
internal/submissions-notes.body:
Name shows differently in the table, username versus submission form name, wrong name
on a submission, file type and size limits on uploads, submission in two sessions has
no time, numbering.

- **"Incomplete registration"** means the user has not filled out and submitted everything
  required by the submission form.
- **"Submission has closed" when following the link:** check the submissions toggle is open
  on your dashboard. If it still happens, contact support.
- **No submission limit on the free version.**
- **Images do not count** toward the abstract word count.
- **Downloading a submission as PDF** is available on paid packages, from the
  Reports & Downloads tab.
- **Only the submitter can edit** their abstract — authors who are not the submitter
  cannot.
- **Controlling edits after acceptance:** use the submission status toggles on your event
  dashboard to decide whether submitters can keep editing.

From a year of support replies, July 2026:

- **The name in the table is not the name on the submission.** The table shows the
  *username* the person gave when they registered their account; the submission form
  holds whatever they typed into the form. The two often differ — most visibly where
  someone has entered their name in a non-Latin script — and it is not a fault. Admins
  cannot change the username; the person updates it themselves under My Profile.
- **File type and size limits on uploads** are per question type and are documented on
  the submission question types guide, under multimedia questions.
- **A submission scheduled in more than one session** only carries individual start and
  end times in the session where it has actually been timed. Seeing blank times against
  a poster that also appears in a teaser session is expected, not a scheduling bug.

internal/symposia-quick-answers.title: Symposia — owners, emails, submission links and closing attachments
internal/symposia-quick-answers.body:
Transfer a symposium to a different organiser, change the symposium owner, symposium
email template, customise the submission URL, people can still attach abstracts to a
symposium, symposium reviewer link, interactive workshop form.

Distilled from support replies in the year to July 2026. Symposia is a separately
purchased add-on, so these come from a smaller group of organisers who ask a lot.

- **Changing who owns a symposium** is done by Oxford Abstracts support — give them
  the symposium number and the new owner's email address. Organisers cannot transfer
  ownership themselves.
- **Symposium emails have their own templates**, separate from the event's ordinary
  email templates. They live on the symposium emails page of the event dashboard, not
  under the main Emails section, which is why people report the templates "missing".
- **Submission URLs cannot be customised.** There is no vanity or branded submission
  link; the system's own URL is what you circulate.
- **People can still attach submissions to a symposium** when the attachments option
  is left open on the symposium dashboard. If submissions keep arriving after you
  meant to stop them, that setting is the cause — turn off allowing submissions to
  the symposium.
- **One reviewer link serves every reviewer.** You do not need a personalised link per
  person: the system decides which submissions to show from the email address they
  signed in with. This worries organisers sending a bulk email; it is correct.

internal/tickets-orders-and-refunds.title: Tickets not showing, group bookings, refunds and what registration cannot do
internal/tickets-orders-and-refunds.body:
Tickets not visible, ticket not showing on the registration page, group booking,
buy tickets for colleagues, refund an attendee, partial refund, bulk import
registrations, check in delegates, reassign a ticket, guest checkout.

Distilled from around 25 support tickets in the year to July 2026.

**Tickets invisible to everyone but you** is nearly always the dates. A ticket is
automatically hidden from non-admins outside its start and end dates, so a start date
in the future — or a past year left on a copied ticket — hides it completely. To test,
switch on the **Admin mode** toggle at the top right of the registration page, or move
the visibility start date into the past. A ticket set "to 1 April" stays on sale until
23:59 that day.

**Group bookings:** selecting more than one ticket reveals name and email fields for
each person. There is a limit of **10 tickets per order**, and every ticket needs a
name and email at purchase — placeholders are fine, and an admin can reassign each
ticket afterwards with the reassign button. Everyone on one order shares a single
order reference, which cannot be split.

**Refunds** return the ticket price **excluding the Oxford Abstracts service fee and
excluding transaction fees**, so the organiser absorbs the service fee on anything
refunded. A partial refund is only possible where an order holds several tickets or
add-ons and one is removed. Payments run through the organiser's own provider, so
Stripe refunds may need doing in Stripe, and the transactions table links straight to
the matching payment there.

**Coupons** are covered in their own note, but two extra points: a coupon must be
applied to *every* ticket type it should cover, or registrants see "code not valid for
selected items"; and a coupon cannot be added once an order is paid — the only route
is refund and rebook.

**Things registration cannot do:**

- **No bulk import of registrants.** Entries are made by hand, or delegates complete
  their own details from their dashboard.
- **No check-in function** at the event.
- **No guest checkout.** Only the ticket details page is public; anyone clicking Get
  Tickets must register or log in first.
- **Tickets cannot be shown to some people and hidden from others.** They are fully
  visible, visible for a period, or admin-only. For a held-back allocation, an admin
  registers people directly.
- **Discount rules** (bulk, package-based percentages) do not exist. Coupons are the
  only mechanism.

**A very small test fee fails** at the payment provider with a 500 error — use at
least 0.50 in the chosen currency.

internal/website-builder-vs-conference-h.title: Website builder or conference homepage — which is which, and can one redirect to the other
internal/website-builder-vs-conference-h.body:
Website builder versus conference homepage, difference between the two sites, redirect
the old homepage to my new website, hide the conference homepage, own domain, multiple
pages, which one do exhibitors and networking live on, virtual.oxfordabstracts.com.

Distilled from support replies in the year to July 2026. Organisers who build a site
with the website builder routinely end up with two public addresses and ask which one
attendees should use.

**They are two different things.**

- **The website builder** produces a public marketing site. It can use your own domain
  and can have as many pages as you like. It is meant to be the public face of the
  conference before and around the event.
- **The conference homepage** sits on an Oxford Abstracts address and is organised as
  tabs rather than pages. It is what an attendee lands on when they log in to the
  event portal, and it is where the conference platform features live — the programme,
  the poster gallery, exhibitor booths and networking.

**Redirecting one to the other is not possible.** The original conference homepage
cannot be pointed at a website-builder site. What you can do instead is **hide** the
conference homepage, so only the built site is public, and let attendees reach the
programme and platform features by logging in once the conference starts.

**So which do you need?** If the question is "I want a proper website with my own
domain", that is the website builder. If it is "I want exhibitor booths, networking or
the poster gallery", those are conference platform features on the Professional
package and are reached through the event portal, not the built site. Wanting both is
normal and does not mean anything is set up wrongly.

internal/what-oxford-abstracts-does-not-.title: Things Oxford Abstracts does not do: visa letters, invitation letters, blind abstract books
internal/what-oxford-abstracts-does-not-.body:
Visa letter, visa invitation letter, letter of invitation, invitation letter for
attendees, can the system generate visa letters, certificate of participation,
attendance letter, anonymous abstract book, hide author names from the abstract book.

Answer these plainly and immediately. A clear no saves a round trip; a vague answer
produces a second ticket. Where there is a real alternative, give it in the same
breath.

**Visa letters and letters of invitation: no.** The system does not generate them, and
this has to be arranged outside Oxford Abstracts. Organisers usually produce them from
their own templates using an export of accepted submitters or registered attendees, so
point them at exporting the list rather than leaving them with a flat no.

**Certificates of participation: yes, but as a paid add-on.** Do not confuse this with
visa letters. Certificates is bought separately and is included with Professional —
see the certificates content, and send pricing questions to the pricing page.

**An abstract book without author names: no.** Author details always appear in an
abstract book and cannot be suppressed. Anyone wanting anonymised material for blind
reviewing should use the reviewing side of the system, where what a reviewer can see is
controlled properly.

**Merging two accounts: no such feature** — see the account and email changes note.

**Partial refunds: not directly** — see the refund article for the two-step method.

**Only the submitter can edit a submission.** Co-authors and panellists cannot upload
files or make changes, however much the organiser wants them to.

A note on the ticket data behind this: the "visa" theme in the gap analysis is mostly
mislabelled. Most of those tickets are about **Visa cards** — expired cards, blocked
payments, "too many card attempts" — and not about visas at all. Card and payment
problems are a registration and payments question; treat them separately.

internal/where-to-find-your-event-id.title: Where do I find my event ID?
internal/where-to-find-your-event-id.body:
Your event ID is the number in the address bar while you are signed in and inside
the event. Look at the URL for `/events/` and take the number straight after it:
in `app.oxfordabstracts.com/admin/events/528/app/...` the event ID is **528**.

It is there on every page inside the event, so any screen will do — the dashboard,
the registrations table, the emails screen. Support often ask for it because it is
the fastest way to be certain which event is being discussed, particularly when an
account runs several with similar names or the same event across multiple years.
